clue.text: Animal rights at first support tag

indicators.note: in a down clue the support is the piece placed underneath, so it comes after the other

parts.note: a tag or name label pinned on is a badge

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word rights

explanation.surface: A campaigner for animal rights pins on a badge showing their support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes R from 'rights'; in a down entry, R 'supporting' BADGE sits beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: The badger is a burrowing black-and-white mammal, so it is a kind of creature.

clue.text: Tables turned round figurehead in city

indicators.note: round says the rearranged letters wrap around the single letter from the figurehead
turned tells us the word Tables is twisted into a new order of letters

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of the word figure is F

explanation.surface: Someone turns the tables on a mere figurehead in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' rearranges TABLES into BELAST, and 'round' puts F (the head of 'figure') inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Belfast is the capital of Northern Ireland, a large urban centre.

clue.text: Rising, when worker takes in sound broadcast

indicators.note: takes in says the first pieces hold another piece inside them

parts.note: when, as in 'as I left', means as
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

indicators.note: sound tells us to use letters that are heard the same as the word given

parts.note: to broadcast is to send out a signal

explanation.surface: A worker tunes in as a sound broadcast goes out on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' signals a homophone of the word meaning broadcast; 'takes in' means the worker and 'when' hold it. 'Rising' is the definition, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascendant star or power is one that is climbing or gaining influence.

clue.text: Farm workers overawe soldiers

parts.note: to cow someone is to overawe or intimidate them
soldiers in the ranks are men

explanation.surface: Labourers on a farm intimidate a troop of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowmen tend cattle, so they are hands employed on a farm.

clue.text: What was left for society girl prior to teacher's return?

indicators.note: prior to places the first piece before the next

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young woman entering high society

indicators.note: return means the word for a teacher is read backwards

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir

explanation.surface: A society girl waits for her teacher to come back to class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses the teacher's form of address, and 'prior to' puts the society girl first; 'What was left' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is the rubble or remains scattered after destruction.

clue.text: Arrangement to meet friend on top of myrtle tree!

parts.note: a date is an appointment to meet someone
a pal is a friend

indicators.note: top of in a down clue means the first letter of the word myrtle

explanation.surface: A couple arrange to meet a friend at the top of a myrtle.
explanation.definitionFit: The date palm is a fruit-bearing palm, a woody plant of desert oases.

clue.text: Single doctor in bad odour might find her attractive!

indicators.note: in places the next pieces inside the letters for bad odour

parts.note: BO stands for body odour, a bad smell
single means one, the Roman numeral I
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A single doctor, despite a bad smell, might still attract a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: 'her' in the surface is the attractive woman the clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bimbo is slang for an attractive but empty-headed young woman.

clue.text: Growth in credit facility

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
facility in the sense of effortlessness is ease

explanation.surface: Growth in a bank's credit facility.
explanation.definitionFit: An increase is a rise or enlargement in amount.

clue.text: One interpretation of "turning aside"

parts.note: one as the article a
a version is one particular reading or interpretation

explanation.surface: A dictionary offering one interpretation of the phrase 'turning aside'.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as A + VERSION; the definition draws on the Latin root avertere, to turn away.
explanation.definitionFit: Aversion originally meant a turning away from something, now a strong dislike.

clue.text: Put up with the way a church accepts order

indicators.note: accepts means the earlier letters take in another piece

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
OM, the Order of Merit, is a British order

explanation.surface: A church's way is to put up with and accept an order.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a British honour; 'accepts' places it inside 'the way a church'.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to tolerate or endure it.

clue.text: Blunder due to foreman not finishing

indicators.note: not finishing says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a gaffer is British slang for a foreman or boss

explanation.surface: A mistake made because the foreman failed to finish the job.
explanation.walkthrough: GAFFER, British slang for a foreman, drops its final R ('not finishing').
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social blunder or embarrassing slip.

clue.text: Speakers' turn of phrase takes one in

definitions.note: the plural possessive stands for a set of small speakers

indicators.note: takes in puts the word one inside the jumbled letters
takes in puts the word one inside the jumbled letters
turn of says the letters of phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A speaker's turn of phrase draws someone in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn of' rearranges the letters of 'phrase' (giving EARPHS) and 'takes in' slips 'one' inside; 'Speakers' are devices, not people talking.
explanation.definitionFit: Earphones are tiny loudspeakers worn over or in the ears.

clue.text: Took in a note

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone receives a note.
explanation.definitionFit: To take in food is to eat, so this is its past tense.

clue.text: Lease protecting right, for example, of occupant

indicators.note: protecting means the first word wraps around and guards the second

parts.note: to lease property is to rent it
right is one example of a side, as is left

explanation.surface: A lease that protects an occupant's rights.
explanation.walkthrough: Right is one example of a side; 'protecting' puts that inside the word for lease.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident is someone who lives in a place, its inhabitant.

clue.text: Whip round — six are generous

indicators.note: round says the word for whip goes around the numeral

parts.note: to lash is to whip
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Six people chip in to a whip-round, being generous.
explanation.walkthrough: A whip-round is a British collection of money among colleagues; here 'round' is the container signal, putting six inside the whip.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavish means extravagantly open-handed, giving freely.

clue.text: Fulminated at poets as they abandon their beliefs

indicators.note: fulminated suggests an explosion, so the letters are blown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone rages at poets for deserting their faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fulminated' rearranges the letters of AT POETS AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostates are people who renounce a religion or principle once held.

clue.text: A long time since switching offices

parts.note: an age is a very long time

indicators.note: switching means the letters of since change places

explanation.surface: It is a long time since anyone switched offices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching' rearranges SINCE into NCIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Agencies are business bureaux or departments providing a service.

clue.text: A good tip is to get down

definitions.meaning: in horse racing a tipster's most confident selection is called this
the soft raised fibres on cloth, its fluffy surface

explanation.surface: Good advice: lie down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is to get' simply links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing tipster's best bet carries this name, and the same word means the fuzzy pile on fabric.

clue.text: Bankers in plane suffer and snore terribly

parts.note: to ail is to suffer or be unwell

indicators.note: terribly signals that the letters of snore are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: On a plane, passengers suffer as someone snores terribly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges SNORE into ERONS; 'Bankers' are things that bank, or tilt, the plane, not money men.
explanation.definitionFit: Ailerons are hinged wing flaps that make an aircraft roll or tilt in a turn.

clue.text: A national leader returned to a measure of power

indicators.note: returned means the leader's letters are read backwards

parts.note: the PM, Prime Minister, leads the nation

explanation.surface: A national leader comes back to power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns PM (Prime Minister) into MP.
explanation.definitionFit: An amp, or ampere, is a unit of electrical current, used loosely for electrical strength.

clue.text: A disease of the foot initially infecting rodent

parts.note: gout often attacks the big toe

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of infecting is used

explanation.surface: A foot disease spreading to a rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: The agouti is a burrowing South American mammal related to the guinea pig.

clue.text: A degree Celsius requires one to wear it!

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: A temperature of one degree means you must wear a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: MAC is short for mackintosh, a British word for a raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A mac is a waterproof coat, something put on to go out in the rain.

clue.text: Vessel found by sanctimonious villain

parts.note: pi is slang for pious or sanctimonious
a rogue is a villain

explanation.surface: A ship discovered by a self-righteous scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirogue is a dugout canoe, a small boat.

clue.text: Collecting for a church service in middle age

parts.note: Mass is the Catholic church service

indicators.note: middle means the central letter of the word age

explanation.surface: Gathering together for church in middle age.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as A MASS IN G, G being the middle of 'age', not a reference to the period of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Amassing means accumulating or gathering a large amount.

clue.text: An ungenerous person that's below average

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece below follows the other

parts.note: the mean is the mathematical average
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A stingy person is one who is below average.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below' works because this is a down entry: 'that's' sits beneath 'average' in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A meanie is a stingy or unkind person, a skinflint.

clue.text: After good notice, acquire device

indicators.note: after places the final piece following the first two

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a newspaper
to get is to acquire

explanation.surface: After seeing a positive advert, someone buys a gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadget is a small mechanical tool or contraption.

clue.text: Conclusion drawn from fashionable railings protecting royal

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: protecting means the railings enclose the royal

parts.note: a fence may be made of railings
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A conclusion drawn from stylish railings around a royal residence.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen; 'protecting' puts the royal inside the railings.
explanation.definitionFit: An inference is a deduction reached by reasoning.

clue.text: Sweetheart burning energy from cream

parts.note: the heart, or centre, of the word sweet is E
something burning is lit
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A sweetheart burns energy eating cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' is the middle letter of 'sweet', not a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of society is its finest, most select group.

clue.text: Miss nothing, being enthusiastic about it

indicators.note: about says the word for keen is wrapped round the letter for nothing

parts.note: avid means keen or enthusiastic
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone eager to miss nothing about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts O (nothing) inside AVID.
explanation.definitionFit: To avoid something is to dodge it or keep clear.

clue.text: One might call for face protection over it

indicators.note: over means the visor fits over, covering it

parts.note: a visor shields the face

explanation.surface: Someone calls for a helmet visor to be pulled over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' means the face protection covers it, so it goes inside; 'One might call' is a visitor, not a phone caller.
explanation.definitionFit: A caller, someone who pays a visit to a home, is a guest.

clue.text: Certain about changing nice but easy job

indicators.note: about says the word for certain goes round the other letters

parts.note: sure means certain

indicators.note: changing signals that the letters of nice are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone is certain to change a nice but undemanding job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges the letters of 'nice' (giving INEC), and 'about' wraps the word for certain round them.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a paid post needing little or no work.

clue.text: Guides, if drug dealers, are executed

indicators.note: executed here means beheaded, so the first letter goes

parts.note: pushers is slang for people who sell drugs

explanation.surface: Drug dealers who are guides being put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are executed' beheads PUSHERS, losing its first letter P.
explanation.definitionFit: Ushers show people to their seats, leading the way.
